title: Cement reaction stoichiometry table
description: Balanced cement and binder reactions with molar masses, per-gram water, CH, heat, molar volumes and chemical shrinkage. Each number is tagged sourced (copied from a source that was opened and read), derived (computed here from sourced numbers and CIAAW atomic weights) or unknown.
disclaimer: Idealised end-state stoichiometry for orientation. Real hydrate compositions, especially C-S-H, AFm, AFt and gels, vary with composition, temperature, w/c and age. Not a substitute for testing or thermodynamic modelling (e.g. GEMS with Cemdata18).

conventions.calorie: 4.184 J (thermochemical calorie) used to convert Lerch & Bogue cal/g values.
conventions.water: Water consumed = H2O written into the balanced products (saturated hydrates), per gram of the key phase.
conventions.chemicalShrinkage: (ΣV reactants incl. liquid water - ΣV products)/mass of key phase, using the molar volumes listed per species (source per value). Positive = volume loss.
conventions.heat: Positive J/g = heat released per gram of the key phase (or the basis stated).

R210.title: Heat of hydration of portland cement pastes (NBS RP684)
R210.used_for: Heats of complete hydration of C3S, beta-C2S, C3A, C4AF (Table 1 and summary); MgO and free CaO values the authors took from the literature; 149 cal/g SO3 for sulfoaluminate formation; 3.7 and 2.7 kcal/mol for hemihydrate and soluble anhydrite to gypsum; clinker test cases (Table 1, series K-3).

R334.title: Cemdata18: A chemical thermodynamic database for hydrated Portland cements and alkali-activated materials
R334.authors: B. Lothenbach, D.A. Kulik, T. Matschei, M. Balonis, L. Baquerizo, B. Dilnesa, G.D. Miron, R.J. Myers
R334.used_for: Standard molar volumes V° (cm3/mol) and enthalpies of formation ΔfH° (kJ/mol) at 25 °C, Tables 1, 3 and 4; statement that calcium carbonate prevents destabilisation of ettringite to monosulfate.

R880.title: Calculation of Cement Composition Using a New Model Compared to the Bogue Model
R880.authors: S.-H. Shim, T.-H. Lee, S.-J. Yang, N.B.Md. Noor, J.-H.-J. Kim
R880.used_for: Bogue equations as given for ASTM C150 including SO3 and CO2 terms, Eqs. (5)-(8).

R330.title: Hydration of calcium sulfoaluminate cements — Experimental findings and thermodynamic modelling
R330.used_for: Ye'elimite hydration with and without calcium sulfate (Eqs. 1-2) and strätlingite formation from belite and AH3 (Eq. 3); strätlingite only stable without portlandite.

R372.title: Calcium aluminate cement conversion analysed by ptychographic nanotomography
R372.authors: S. Shirani, A. Cuesta, A.G. De la Torre, A. Diaz, P. Trtik, M. Holler, M.A.G. Aranda
R372.used_for: CA hydration and conversion reactions (1)-(5) with molar masses, densities, molar volumes and theoretical chemical shrinkage / secondary porosity (Tables 1-2).

R1882.title: Hydration reactions in portland cement-silica fume blends
R1882.used_for: Cement, silica fume and fly ash oxide analyses and Bogue phases (Table I); Ca(OH)2 contents of plain and silica-fume pastes (test cases).

R3883.title: A model for two types of calcium silicate hydrate in the microstructure of Portland cement pastes
R3883.used_for: Hydration reactions Eqs. (1)-(6) with C3.4S2H8 (=C1.7SH4) C-S-H; densities and molar masses (Table 1); saturated C-S-H density 1990 kg/m3; Avrami constants for degree of hydration by phase (Table 2).

R3079.title: Advances in understanding ye'elimite-rich cements
R3079.used_for: Context only: CAH10 can form with ettringite and AH3 when calcium sulfate is low; AH3 gel density about 1.5 g/cm3 in CSA paste versus 2.40 g/cm3 for gibbsite.

NEW-BENTZ-2005.title: CEMHYD3D: A Three-Dimensional Cement Hydration and Microstructure Development Modeling Package. Version 3.0 (NIST IR 7232)
NEW-BENTZ-2005.used_for: Molar volumes, specific gravities and heats of formation of cement phases and hydrates as coded in disrealnew.c (Appendix B, after Fukuhara et al. 1981); pozzolanic C1.1SH3.9 product; 780 J/g silica fume, 800 J/g slag, 800 J/g AS heats; slag hydration product stoichiometries (Table 2) and slagchar.dat example.

NEW-BENTZ-2009.title: Limestone Fillers Conserve Cement; Part 1: An analysis based on Powers' model
NEW-BENTZ-2009.authors: D.P. Bentz, E.F. Irassar, B.E. Bucher, W.J. Weiss
NEW-BENTZ-2009.used_for: Powers' model volume fractions with Jensen & Hansen parameters (non-evaporable water 0.23, chemical shrinkage 0.064, gel water 0.19 g/g), inert limestone filler, and worked results (w/c 0.356, 0.42, 8.7 % porosity, w/cm 0.338-0.267).

NEW-LEON-CHEN-2021.title: Thermal Analysis of Mass Concrete Containing Ground Granulated Blast Furnace Slag
NEW-LEON-CHEN-2021.used_for: Secondary citation of Schindler & Folliard (2005): ultimate heat of GGBFS 461 J/g (Grade 100) and 550 J/g (Grade 120).
